name: Bank reconciliations not independently reviewed -> undetected bank errors
rationale: The bank reconciliation is the key detective control over cash; without independent review, errors and irregularities go unchallenged. The rule directs the auditor to test the review control, reperform the reconciliation, vouch aged items, and obtain direct bank confirmation.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

name: Unusual payments to unfamiliar beneficiaries -> improper payment risk
rationale: Payments to unfamiliar beneficiaries bypass the implicit control of a known supplier relationship. The rule directs full-population beneficiary analysis, vouching of unusual payments to supporting documents, and tracing of new beneficiaries to verification evidence.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

name: Year-end bank transfers -> cut-off and double-counting risk
rationale: Transfers in transit at year-end can be double-counted or omitted, and may be used to window-dress liquidity. The rule directs cut-off testing that matches both sides of every material transfer to bank value dates and reperforms the in-transit position.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

name: Cash not physically verified -> existence risk for cash on hand
rationale: Cash is the most portable asset; without independent physical verification, shortages accumulate undetected. The rule directs surprise physical verification by the auditor, reconciliation of the count to records, and testing of the entity's own count controls.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

name: Lack of segregation of duties -> misappropriation fraud risk
rationale: Incompatible functions in one person's hands remove the independent check between a transaction and its concealment - the classic opportunity condition for asset misappropriation. Fraud rules run first (priority 5) so fraud-focused responses are planned before standard procedures.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

name: Aggressive earnings-linked incentives -> fictitious revenue fraud risk
rationale: Material rewards tied to aggressive targets create the incentive condition for fraudulent revenue reporting. Fraud rules run first (priority 5) so fraud-focused responses are planned before standard procedures.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

name: Opaque related-party structures -> journal manipulation fraud risk
rationale: Undocumented related-party structures provide the channels through which manipulated journals and off-book arrangements flow. Fraud rules run first (priority 5).
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

name: Covenant pressure -> estimate bias fraud risk
rationale: Threatened loss of financing concentrates pressure on period-end balances and the estimates that determine them. Fraud rules run first (priority 5).
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

name: Finance turnover -> misappropriation fraud risk
rationale: Instability in finance weakens review disciplines and creates gaps in which diversion and concealment go unchallenged. Fraud rules run first (priority 5).
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

name: Rationalised aggressive accounting -> journal manipulation fraud risk
rationale: A culture that normalises aggressive accounting blurs the boundary between aggressive and improper - the observable form of rationalization. Fraud rules run first (priority 5).
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

name: Weak cash oversight -> misappropriation fraud risk
rationale: Material cash volumes without independent oversight are a direct opportunity for diversion, and cash leaves little trail. Fraud rules run first (priority 5).
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

name: No trusted whistleblowing channel -> journal manipulation fraud risk
rationale: Without a safe reporting route, observed wrongdoing - especially involving management - goes unreported, removing a key deterrent and detection channel. Fraud rules run first (priority 5).
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

name: Undocumented manual journals -> occurrence and accuracy risk
rationale: Supporting documentation is what allows a journal to be vouched to a genuine event; without it the auditor cannot distinguish valid adjustments from invented ones. The rule directs the auditor to vouch journals to support, test the approval control, and scan the full population for unusual entries - treating unsupported journals as exceptions to investigate, never as proof of misstatement or of fraud.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

name: Management override capability -> fraud risk responses
rationale: Those who design and oversee controls can bypass them, so normal controls provide no protection against override. The rule directs the auditor to the specific responses override requires: targeted journal-entry testing, inquiries of those charged with governance, and evaluation of estimates for bias - while preserving the distinction between opportunity, suspected indicator and confirmed fraud. v2: excludes F-FRP-001 - when unsupported manual journals are also present, the narrower RULE-FRP-002B (priority 5) fires instead, adding the journal-testing battery without duplicating the override procedures.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

name: Override plus undocumented journals -> intensified journal testing
rationale: Management override capability combined with a population of undocumented manual journals is the highest-risk combination in financial reporting: the means (override) and the vehicle (unsupported journals) are both present. The narrower rule takes precedence over the general override rule and adds the full journal-testing battery - vouching, approval testing and population scanning - to the override procedures.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

name: No related-party identification -> disclosure completeness risk
rationale: A related-party transaction can only be correctly measured and disclosed if it is first recognised as related-party. The rule directs the auditor to inspect the claimed population, to independently search for what the entity's process missed, and to test the substance, measurement and disclosure of what is found.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

name: Unsupported provision assumptions -> measurement and completeness risk
rationale: A provision is only as good as its assumptions; undocumented assumptions cannot be distinguished from biased ones. The rule directs the auditor to challenge each key assumption against evidence, to recalculate and sensitivity-test the amounts, and to search for obligations never provided for - developing an independent expectation rather than accepting management's number.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

name: No disclosure completeness process -> omitted disclosures risk
rationale: Disclosures do not affect the trial balance, so they are missed without a disciplined process. The rule directs the auditor to act as the missing control: complete an independent disclosure checklist, trace disclosed amounts to the records, and assess novel transactions for disclosure implications.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

name: Telecom towers and network sites carry dismantling and site-restoration (decommissioning) obligations -> Decommissioning provision omitted or understated; related asset-retirement cost not capitalised
rationale: A large, dispersed site estate makes decommissioning obligations easy to overlook, so the rule directs the auditor first to the completeness of the obligation population (contracts to register) and then to measurement.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

name: Multi-element customer contracts (handset plus service bundles) -> Incorrect allocation of consideration across bundle components and premature revenue recognition
rationale: Allocation error is systematic rather than random, so the rule focuses on reperforming the allocation logic on new plans and testing the approval control that authorises the inputs.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

name: High-volume automated billing with complex rating and tariff logic -> Systematic billing errors from rating or tariff configuration
rationale: Because one defect replicates across millions of transactions, the rule emphasises independent reperformance and exception follow-up over vouching individual bills.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

name: Work in progress with absorbed production overheads -> Misallocated overheads and misstated work in progress
rationale: Overhead valuation fails at the rate-setting stage, so the rule leads with reperformance of the model and a physical reality check on WIP stages.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

name: Standard costing with material variances not investigated -> Variances buried rather than analysed, misstating inventory and cost of sales
rationale: Variances are the costing system's built-in diagnostic, so the rule treats them as the primary evidence and tests both their investigation and their accounting.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

name: Warranty obligations on goods sold -> Understated warranty provision
rationale: Warranty estimates live or die on claim experience, so the rule centres on back-testing and cohort analysis rather than accepting the model.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

name: High-volume cash and card sales with shrinkage exposure -> Unrecorded sales and theft of takings (shrinkage)
rationale: Cash volume is the risk driver, so the rule focuses on the till-to-bank trail and outlet-level analytics rather than individual transaction vouching.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

name: Supplier rebates and promotional income -> Premature or overstated recognition of supplier rebates
rationale: Supplier agreement is the key uncertainty, so the rule emphasises vouching to signed terms and external confirmation.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

name: Gift cards sold and loyalty points outstanding -> Understated deferred revenue from unredeemed gift cards and loyalty points
rationale: The liability is the risk, so the rule works from the liability population outward: reconcile it, then test releases and breakage.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

name: Loan book subject to expected credit losses -> Understated loan impairment (expected credit losses)
rationale: ECL fails at staging and parameter judgments, so the rule targets borderline cases and overlays rather than re-running the whole model naively.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

name: Interest income recognised on non-performing loans -> Overstated interest income on non-performing loans
rationale: Accrual is automatic and stopping it is the decision, so the rule tests the suspension boundary and the provision against continuing accruals.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

name: Complex treasury and financial instruments -> Misclassification and valuation error in financial instruments
rationale: Information asymmetry is the core problem, so the rule prioritises independent challenge of inputs and classification over accepting model outputs.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

name: Inadequate warehouse security -> inventory loss risk
rationale: Unrestricted physical access removes the main barrier to unauthorised removal of goods, so recorded quantities may exceed quantities actually held. The rule directs the auditor to existence-focused substantive procedures and to test the completeness of loss records, with explicit per-assertion reasoning.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

name: Terminated employees remain on payroll -> ghost employee risk
rationale: A lag between termination and removal from the payroll master, combined with bulk electronic payments, creates the opportunity for continued payments to non-employees. The rule directs occurrence-focused testing: analytical scans, tracing leavers, and vouching payees to employment evidence.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

name: No segregation of payroll duties -> fictitious payee risk
rationale: Combined control of employee master records and payment processing removes the primary barrier to creating fictitious payees. The rule directs the auditor to test access rights, vouch master changes to independent approval, and scan for fictitious-employee indicators.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

name: Overtime not independently approved -> inflated overtime risk
rationale: Without independent approval there is no check that overtime was worked or necessary, particularly where hours are self-reported. The rule directs vouching of overtime to approved timesheets corroborated by attendance records, plus analytical procedures to find concentrations.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

name: Incorrect payroll calculations -> misstated wages and deductions
rationale: Errors in rates, tax tables or deduction parameters flow systematically into pay and related liabilities. The rule directs independent recalculation from authorised sources, agreement of rates, and reconciliation of payroll to the ledger.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

name: Repairs capitalised without assessment -> classification and valuation risk
rationale: Capitalisation without documented assessment against clear criteria is a recognised source of misclassification between expense and asset. The rule directs the auditor to test the classification boundary substantively (vouching near-boundary items), to inspect the policy and approval controls, and to use analytical procedures to spot systematic shifts - with per-assertion reasoning explaining why classification and valuation are affected.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

name: Unreviewed depreciation parameters -> charge and carrying amount risk
rationale: Depreciation parameters set in the past drift from economic reality without periodic review. The rule directs the auditor beyond arithmetical accuracy (recalculation) to the appropriateness of the parameters themselves (evaluation against usage, condition and industry practice), plus testing of change controls.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

name: Disposals not communicated -> existence risk for recorded assets
rationale: When operations can dispose of assets without finance being informed, the register retains assets that no longer exist. The rule directs the auditor to direct existence testing (physical verification from the register), to test recorded disposals, and to actively search for unrecorded disposals.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

name: No impairment indicator process -> unrecognised impairment risk
rationale: Impairment is only recognised if indicators are first noticed; without a process to look for them, carrying amounts can remain overstated. The rule directs the auditor to evaluate management's assessment (or its absence), to independently identify indicators through analytical procedures, and to test measurement where indicators exist.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

name: Replaced components not derecognised -> double-counted carrying amount
rationale: Capitalising a replacement without derecognising the replaced part counts the same economic capacity twice. The rule directs the auditor to trace replacement work orders to derecognition entries, to test componentisation, and to corroborate the work through observation.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

name: Unmatched supplier invoices -> invalid purchase risk
rationale: Without matching to receipt evidence, nothing stops invoices for goods never delivered from being recorded and paid. The rule directs vouching to GRNs, a test of the matching control, and follow-up of the exception population most at risk.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

name: Late supplier invoices -> unrecorded liabilities risk
rationale: A liability exists on receipt, not on invoicing; late invoices therefore create unrecorded liabilities. The rule directs two-directional cut-off testing around GRNs and inspection of management's accrual, targeting completeness and cut-off.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

name: Uncontrolled supplier master changes -> fictitious supplier risk
rationale: Master data decides who gets paid and into which account, so uncontrolled changes create both error and fraud opportunity. The rule directs a test of the approval control, substantive vouching of payments to new or changed suppliers, and full-population analysis for fictitious-supplier indicators.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

name: Duplicate invoice processing -> duplicate recording risk
rationale: A second recording of the same invoice is not a second purchase, and a second payment is a cash loss. The rule directs full-population duplicate analysis, documentary resolution of each suspected duplicate, and a test of the paid-invoice control.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

name: Wrong-period purchase recording -> cut-off risk
rationale: The correct period for a purchase is determined by receipt, not by invoice processing. The rule directs two-directional cut-off testing, GRN tracing for completeness, and trend analysis to focus testing on the months most at risk.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

name: Premature revenue recognition -> revenue overstatement risk
rationale: Recording revenue before the recognition criteria are met breaks the link between the entry and the underlying event, so recorded revenue may be overstated (occurrence) and in the wrong period (cut-off). The rule directs the auditor to occurrence-focused vouching, contract inspection and cut-off testing, plus a test of the preventive matching control.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

name: Late-recorded dispatches -> revenue understatement (cut-off) risk
rationale: When dispatch precedes invoicing across the reporting date, earned sales fall out of the current period. The rule directs two-directional cut-off testing and inspection of management's own reconciliation, targeting completeness and cut-off of revenue.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

name: Unsupported sales -> fictitious revenue risk
rationale: Dispatch or performance evidence connects a recorded sale to a real event; without it the auditor cannot distinguish missing paperwork from a sale that never happened. The rule directs vouching to supporting evidence, analytical comparison with operational data, and external confirmation for independent corroboration.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

name: Revenue-linked incentives -> fraud risk over revenue
rationale: Material revenue-linked incentives give management a motive to manipulate revenue, and manual journals and period-end discretion provide the opportunity. The rule directs analytics tied to target mechanics, journal entry testing, and corroborated inquiry - with explicit warnings against presuming fraud.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

name: Unusual year-end transactions -> validity and cut-off risk
rationale: Non-routine transactions bypass normal processing controls and their year-end timing can be chosen for effect. The rule directs the auditor to understand each transaction's substance, corroborate it with independent evidence, and scan the full population so unusual items are not missed.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
